notes: Each automated check id maps to a method on tests/Compliance/GuidelineScanner.php. Run: vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit.unit.xml.dist --filter WpOrgGuidelinesTest

guidelines.title: Plugins must be compatible with the GNU General Public License
guidelines.summary: All code, data, images and third-party material must be GPL-compatible.

checks.description: Plugin header and readme declare a GPL-2.0-or-later license; LICENSE.txt is present.
Every bundled third-party library and font set ships its license file.

guidelines.title: Developers are responsible for the contents and actions of their plugins
guidelines.summary: Every file must comply; licensing of all files and the terms of third-party APIs must be verified.

checks.description: Review third-party API terms (Sender.net, Mandrill) and confirm every bundled asset's license before each release.

guidelines.title: A stable version of a plugin must be available from its WordPress Plugin Directory page
guidelines.summary: The directory copy is the one WordPress.org distributes; it must be kept current.

checks.description: readme Stable tag == plugin header Version == CERTIFICATE_GENERATOR_VERSION == Config::VERSION == top readme changelog entry.

guidelines.title: Code must be (mostly) human readable
guidelines.summary: No obfuscation; source and build tools must be publicly available.

checks.description: No eval, base64_decode, gzinflate, gzuncompress, str_rot13 or create_function in shipped code.
readme.txt links the public development location.
Minified files only appear in bundled vendor libraries that ship a license/source reference.

guidelines.title: Trialware is not permitted
guidelines.summary: No locked features, trial periods or quotas that require payment to unlock.

checks.description: Shipped code contains no license/plan gating or quota-lock wording.

guidelines.title: Software as a Service is permitted
guidelines.summary: External services must provide real functionality and be documented in the readme.

checks.description: Every hard-coded outbound host appears in the readme's External services section.

guidelines.title: Plugins may not track users without their consent
guidelines.summary: No contact with external servers or data collection without explicit, opt-in consent.

checks.description: Same check as G6: outbound calls only to documented, user-configured services.
No analytics/telemetry endpoints or usage reporting in shipped code.

guidelines.title: Plugins may not send executable code via third-party systems
guidelines.summary: No remote JS/CSS, no updates or installs from outside WordPress.org.

checks.description: wp_enqueue_*/wp_register_* never load a remote URL; no script/link tags pointing off-site.
No custom update checkers (update_plugins transient filters, plugin-update-checker).

guidelines.title: Developers and their plugins must not do anything illegal, dishonest, or morally offensive
guidelines.summary: No fake reviews, SEO abuse, keyword stuffing, botnets or misleading claims.

checks.description: Readme claims are accurate; no review manipulation or misleading marketing.

guidelines.title: Plugins may not embed external links or credits on the public site without explicit permission
guidelines.summary: "Powered by" credits must be opt-in and off by default.

checks.description: No 'powered by' credit in shipped output.

guidelines.title: Plugins should not hijack the admin dashboard
guidelines.summary: Upsells and notices must be limited, dismissible, and used sparingly.

checks.description: Every notice printed from an admin_notices callback is dismissible or limited to the plugin's own screens.

guidelines.title: Public facing pages on WordPress.org (readmes) must not spam
guidelines.summary: Readmes are for people: no keyword stuffing, at most 5 tags, accurate headers.

checks.description: Required readme headers present, <= 5 tags, short description <= 150 characters, plugin name matches the header.

guidelines.title: Plugins must use WordPress' default libraries
guidelines.summary: Libraries shipped with WordPress (jQuery, PHPMailer, SimplePie...) must not be bundled.

checks.description: No copies of WordPress-bundled libraries in the shipped files.

guidelines.title: Frequent commits to a plugin should be avoided
guidelines.summary: The SVN repository is for releases, not development.

checks.description: Only commit tagged releases to WordPress.org SVN; develop on GitHub.

guidelines.title: Plugin version numbers must be incremented for each new release
guidelines.summary: Each release needs a higher version number.

checks.description: Same check as G3.
Version is a dotted numeric version (x.y.z).

guidelines.title: A complete plugin must be available at the time of submission
guidelines.summary: Names cannot be reserved; the submitted plugin must work.

checks.description: Main plugin file header has Plugin Name, Description, Version, Requires at least, Requires PHP, Author, License and Text Domain.

guidelines.title: Plugins must respect trademarks, copyrights, and project names
guidelines.summary: A slug may not begin with another product's trademark.

checks.description: Slug / text domain does not begin with a known trademarked term.

guidelines.title: We reserve the right to maintain the Plugin Directory to the best of our ability
guidelines.summary: WordPress.org may update guidelines and act at its discretion.

checks.description: Re-read the guidelines before each release; update this file when they change.

guidelines.title: Review team: unique, prefixed names
guidelines.summary: All global functions, classes, constants, options, transients, hooks, AJAX actions, cron hooks and shortcodes use a unique prefix of at least 4 characters.

checks.description: Global functions start with certificate_generator_, classes with CertificateGenerator, constants with CERTIFICATE_GENERATOR_ (namespaced code, lib/ and vendor/ exempt).
Options, transients, fired hooks, AJAX actions, cron hooks and shortcodes start with certificate_generator_.

guidelines.title: Review team: block direct file access
guidelines.summary: Every PHP file with executable code exits when ABSPATH is not defined.

checks.description: Every shipped PHP file with top-level executable code checks ABSPATH.

guidelines.title: Review team: internationalisation
guidelines.summary: Translatable strings use the plugin slug as text domain.

checks.description: Every gettext call passes the literal text domain certificate-generator.

guidelines.title: Review team: do not load WordPress core files directly
guidelines.summary: No includes of wp-load.php / wp-config.php.

checks.description: No include/require of wp-load.php or wp-config.php.

guidelines.title: Review team: no debug output in production
guidelines.summary: No unconditional error_log / var_dump / print_r output.

checks.description: error_log only inside the WP_DEBUG-gated logger; no var_dump or echoed print_r.

guidelines.title: Review team: Plugin Check
guidelines.summary: The official Plugin Check reports no errors on the release ZIP.

checks.description: Build the ZIP (composer zip), copy it to a test site as plugins/certificate-generator (inactive), run: wp plugin check certificate-generator. Expect 0 errors.
